title: Ezekiel Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 22.

questions.question: What did the LORD tell Ezekiel to show the bloody city?
questions.explanation: The LORD instructed Ezekiel to show her all her abominations (Ezekiel 22:2).

questions.question: What has the city done in the midst of it according to Ezekiel 22?
questions.explanation: The city is said to shed blood in the midst of it (Ezekiel 22:3).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 22:4, what have the people become guilty of?
questions.explanation: The verse states they have become guilty in the blood that they have shed (Ezekiel 22:4).

questions.question: True or False: The princes of Israel used their power to protect the innocent.
questions.explanation: The princes were in the city to their power to shed blood (Ezekiel 22:6), indicating they did not protect the innocent.

questions.question: What did the people do to the fatherless and the widow according to Ezekiel 22:7?
questions.explanation: The verse states they vexed the fatherless and the widow (Ezekiel 22:7).

questions.question: True or False: The people of the city despised the holy things of the LORD.
questions.explanation: The verse states that they have despised the holy things and profaned the sabbaths (Ezekiel 22:8).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 22:9, what kind of lewd acts did men commit?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that in thee they eat upon the mountains and commit lewdness (Ezekiel 22:9).

questions.question: What did the people do with their father's nakedness according to Ezekiel 22:10?
questions.explanation: The verse states that they have discovered their fathers' nakedness (Ezekiel 22:10).

questions.question: True or False: The people have only oppressed their neighbors and not the strangers.
questions.explanation: The verse indicates they have dealt by oppression with the stranger (Ezekiel 22:7).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 22:11, what abomination is mentioned?
questions.explanation: The verse states that one hath committed abomination with his neighbour's wife (Ezekiel 22:11).

questions.question: In what order is the city judged according to Ezekiel 22?
questions.explanation: The judgment focuses on shedding blood as a primary offense (Ezekiel 22:3-4).

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What has Israel become according to Ezekiel 22:18?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:18 states, 'the house of Israel is to me become dross.' This indicates a loss of purity and value, as dross is the waste material separated from metals during refining.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 22:12, what have the people taken to shed blood?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:12 says, 'In thee have they taken gifts to shed blood,' indicating that corruption and wrongdoing were incentivized by bribery.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel are described as having oppressed the poor and needy in Ezekiel 22:29.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:29 explicitly states, 'the people of the land have used oppression, and exercised robbery, and have vexed the poor and needy,' confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: What does God promise to do in Ezekiel 22:15?
options: Consume their filthiness out of them
Make them a great nation again
questions.correctAnswer: Consume their filthiness out of them
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 22:15, God states, 'I will consume thy filthiness out of thee,' indicating a process of purification and judgment.

questions.question: What analogy is used in Ezekiel 22:20 to describe God's gathering of the people?
options: As silver is gathered into the furnace
questions.correctAnswer: As silver is gathered into the furnace
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:20 states, 'As they gather silver, and brass, and iron, and lead, and tin, into the midst of the furnace,' illustrating God's intention to purify through trials.

questions.question: True or False: In Ezekiel 22:26, the priests are said to have shown a clear difference between the holy and the profane.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:26 says, 'they have put no difference between the holy and profane,' indicating that the priests failed to uphold God's standards.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 22:14 question about the people's hearts and hands?
options: Their strength in the days of God's dealing
questions.correctAnswer: Their strength in the days of God's dealing
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:14 asks, 'Can thine heart endure, or can thine hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal with thee?' This emphasizes the challenge they will face during God's judgment.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 22:21, what does God say He will do to the people?
options: Melt them in the fire of His wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Melt them in the fire of His wrath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:21 states, 'I will gather you, and blow upon you in the fire of my wrath, and ye shall be melted in the midst thereof,' indicating severe judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 22:27, how are the princes described?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:27 describes the princes as 'like wolves ravening the prey,' indicating their predatory and destructive behavior.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 22:19 summarize the condition of the people?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:19 states, 'Because ye are all become dross,' summarizing the people's moral and spiritual degradation.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 22:30 mentions that God sought for a man to stand in the gap, but found none.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:30 confirms this by stating, 'I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me... but I found none.'

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Ezekiel 22:31 for the people's actions?
options: They will be judged with fire
questions.correctAnswer: They will be judged with fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:31 states, 'I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath,' indicating the severe consequence for their actions.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 22.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will happen to the people of Israel for their transgressions?
options: They will be gathered and judged
They will be returned to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They will be gathered and judged
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He will gather them in His anger and fury, and they shall be melted in the midst of the furnace, indicating judgment for their sins (Ezekiel 22:20-21).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 22, what did the princes of Israel do?
options: Shed blood and sought dishonest gain
Cared for the widows and orphans
questions.correctAnswer: Shed blood and sought dishonest gain
questions.explanation: Ezekiel describes the princes as being like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls to get dishonest gain (Ezekiel 22:27).

questions.question: What did the prophets do according to Ezekiel 22:28?
questions.explanation: The prophets are accused of daubing the people with untempered mortar, seeing vanity, and divining lies unto them, claiming to speak for the LORD when He had not spoken (Ezekiel 22:28).

questions.question: What was the condition of the land as described in Ezekiel 22:24?
options: It was not cleansed and lacked rain
It was a land of peace
It was a sanctuary for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: It was not cleansed and lacked rain
questions.explanation: The LORD tells Ezekiel to say that the land is not cleansed nor rained upon in the day of indignation, reflecting its moral and spiritual desolation (Ezekiel 22:24).

questions.question: What role did the priests play in the corruption of the land?
options: They upheld the law and sanctified the people
They violated the law and profaned holy things
They offered sacrifices to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They violated the law and profaned holy things
questions.explanation: Ezekiel states that the priests have violated God's law and profaned His holy things, not distinguishing between the holy and the profane (Ezekiel 22:26).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 22:30, what was the LORD seeking among the people?
options: A prophet to speak on their behalf
A man to stand in the gap
A warrior to defend the city
questions.correctAnswer: A man to stand in the gap
questions.explanation: The LORD sought for a man among them to make up the hedge and stand in the gap before Him for the land, indicating the need for intercession (Ezekiel 22:30).

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 22:31 indicate about the consequence of the people's actions?
options: They will be spared from destruction
They will face the fire of God's wrath
They will be gathered into safety
questions.correctAnswer: They will face the fire of God's wrath
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD has poured out His indignation upon them and consumed them with the fire of His wrath as a consequence of their sin (Ezekiel 22:31).

questions.question: True or False: The people of the land have treated the poor and needy with kindness.
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the people have used oppression and exercised robbery, vexing the poor and needy (Ezekiel 22:29), indicating their mistreatment of these vulnerable groups.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD found a man among the people to stand in the gap.
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He sought for a man to stand in the gap but found none, indicating a lack of righteous leaders (Ezekiel 22:30).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God's judgment against corruption in leadership?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:23 similarly condemns the rulers and leaders for being corrupt and failing to care for the widows and orphans, reflecting the theme found in Ezekiel 22.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'dross' as used in Ezekiel 22:18?
questions.explanation: The term 'dross' refers to the worthless material that is separated from metal during the refining process, indicating that the house of Israel has become worthless due to their sins (Ezekiel 22:18).

questions.question: In what way does Ezekiel 22:26 relate to the New Testament teaching on discernment?
options: It encourages strict adherence to rituals
It promotes the idea of being 'doers of the word'
questions.explanation: The violation of the law by the priests in Ezekiel 22:26 parallels the New Testament warnings about false teachers and the need for discernment among believers (e.g., Matthew 7:15).

questions.question: How does the imagery of fire in Ezekiel 22:21 connect to biblical themes of purification?
options: It represents God's judgment without restoration
It indicates a complete abandonment by God
questions.explanation: The use of fire in the context of judgment indicates a process of purification and refinement, similar to how God uses trials to refine His people throughout Scripture (Ezekiel 22:21).

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 22:2 indicate about the city that the Lord commands Ezekiel to judge?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:2 states, 'Now, thou son of man, wilt thou judge, wilt thou judge the bloody city? yea, thou shalt shew her all her abominations.' This indicates that the city is characterized by violence and bloodshed.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 22:12, what unethical practices had the people engaged in?
options: They took gifts to shed blood
questions.correctAnswer: They took gifts to shed blood
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:12 reveals that 'In thee have they taken gifts to shed blood; thou hast taken usury and increase...' indicating their corrupt practices.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized in Ezekiel 22:14 regarding His judgment?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 22:14, God proclaims His intention to deal with the city, reflecting His attribute of justice as He cannot overlook sin.

questions.question: What does the metaphor of dross in Ezekiel 22:18 signify about the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:18 states, 'the house of Israel is to me become dross...' indicating their degraded state and lack of value due to sin.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 22:30 reveal about God's desire for the people of Israel?
options: He seeks a man to stand in the gap
He wants them to continue in sin
questions.correctAnswer: He seeks a man to stand in the gap
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:30 expresses God's search for someone to intercede for the land, showing His desire for repentance and restoration rather than judgment.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 22:26, what sin is attributed to the priests of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:26 states, 'Her priests have violated my law, and have profaned mine holy things...' indicating their failure to uphold God's standards.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Ezekiel 22:4 and 22:5 convey about the city's reputation?
options: It is a reproach to nations
It is a city of peace
questions.correctAnswer: It is a reproach to nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:4 and 22:5 together depict the city as guilty and infamous, making it a reproach to the heathen, indicating its disgraceful state.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 22:21 indicate about God's actions towards the people?
options: He will gather and melt them in His wrath
He will protect them from enemies
He will lead them to repentance
questions.correctAnswer: He will gather and melt them in His wrath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:21 states, 'Yea, I will gather you, and blow upon you in the fire of my wrath, and ye shall be melted...' indicating God's judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 22:24 describe the state of the land at the time of God's indignation?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:24 describes the land as 'the land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation', highlighting its spiritual barrenness.

questions.question: What is the implication of the conspiracy among the prophets mentioned in Ezekiel 22:25?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:25 states, 'There is a conspiracy of her prophets... they have devoured souls...', indicating that they are misleading the people.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I have poured out my fury' in Ezekiel 22:22 teach about God's response to sin?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:22 states, 'ye shall know that I the LORD have poured out my fury upon you,' underscoring God's active and just response to sin.

questions.question: What does the behavior of the princes in Ezekiel 22:27 reveal about societal leadership?
options: They are protectors of the weak
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:27 describes the princes as 'like wolves ravening the prey', which reveals their corrupt nature and exploitation of the vulnerable.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 22:6 imply about the power dynamics among the leaders of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:6 states, 'the princes of Israel, every one were in thee to their power to shed blood,' indicating their abuse of power.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is unjust in His punishment of Israel. What does Ezekiel 22:31 actually teach?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 22:31 states, 'Therefore have I poured out mine indignation upon them; I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath...' indicating that their actions warranted God's judgment.
